title: Auth session inversion during hotpatch causes cross-customer credential confusion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported sporadic authorization failures followed by unexpected access to resources belonging to other customers after a hotpatch rolled into Dedicated and Private clusters. Impact: token refresh sequences occasionally returned API keys/org-scoped sessions that belonged to a different tenant resulting in temporary cross-customer request acceptance, observed across Hosted/Dedicated/Private but amplified on Dedicated pools with connection reuse. Repro steps (high level): 1) Customer A sends long-running streaming generation. 2) Their backend triggers token refresh while a leader election/hotpatch completes on the sidecar auth-sync. 3) Gateway reuses a connection where the session_binding slot had been updated out-of-order; subsequent requests carried a mismatched tenant header. Environments affected: dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (primary), a subset of private on-prem gateways where sticky-connection pooling is enabled. Initial hypothesis: a hotpatch that changed the token-refresh cache eviction/merge ordering introduced a race where session binding updates are non-atomic and the code path that prefers local KV state can invert tenant affinity under concurrent refreshes. This interacts with our connection pool reuse optimization which does not re-validate per-connection tenant tags on eviction.
steps_taken: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Pager duty: Incident declared after support ticket SUP-2024 and SUP-2025 escalations; on-call (Marco) paged.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Immediate mitigation: toggled feature flag `auth.sticky_connection_opt` to false globally for Dedicated and Private clusters to force per-request validation; coordinated with Platform to apply to affected regions.
2026-03-10 10:30 - Rotated API keys for two impacted customers as out-of-band precaution (customer-approved) and created temporary allowlist/denylist entries in gateway routing.
2026-03-11 14:20 - Reproduced locally with a stress harness that simulates concurrent refresh + connection reuse; confirmed session-binding inversion when cache merge uses non-atomic write path.

2026-03-12 08:05 - Drafted a fix: replace non-atomic merge with CAS-based update flow + add per-connection tenant tag validation on checkout; added assertions to reject requests with tenant-header mismatch.
2026-03-12 19:00 - Security notified; initial CVSS-style assessment completed; recommended expedited patch and coordination with Trust & Safety for customer outreach.
2026-03-13 02:15 - Small hotfix branch opened and tested in staging under high-concurrency conditions; no cross-tenant acceptance observed in 48-hour run.
2026-03-14 07:50 - PR opened and submitted for review: runtime PR 7891; assigned reviewers from infra and security.
2026-03-14 11:10 - Canary plan approved: 10% of Dedicated clusters + 2 Private customer testbeds for 12 hours, monitor tenancy-assertion metrics and SLO error rates.
proposed_fix: Implement atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) for session table updates during refresh flows and reintroduce a strict per-connection tenant tag validation on connection checkout. Remove the optimization that allows write-order inversion during cache merge. Add integration tests that simulate concurrent refresh + connection reuse, and unit tests for tenant assertion logic.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR 7891 to main after 2 approvals and security sign-off.
2) Deploy to staging, run 48-hour stress test against reproducer harness.
3) Canary deploy to 10% of Dedicated clusters and 2 Private customer sandboxes for 12 hours.
4) Monitor metrics and error budgets; if stable, roll out to remaining Dedicated clusters during low-traffic window.
5) For Hosted API, deploy a coordinated patch with database migration script to ensure backward compatibility and run canary for 4 hours.
6) Post-incident customer communication and rotate any keys if requested by customers or Trust & Safety.
7) Postmortem and follow-ups: add invariant checks, backfill tests, and update runbook.
monitoring: Quick query: SELECT count(*) FROM auth_events WHERE tenant_header != session_binding AND env IN ('dedicated','private') GROUP BY 1 - run every 5m on OLAP dashboard
Trace sample: collect full traces for requests where tenant_assertion_fail == true, preserve headers for debugging (redact secrets).
